answer: A trust-graph routing protocol curbs Sybil attacks by dispatching bounded random walks across peer attestations. As validation probes wander through a clustered lotus network, sparse cut bottlenecks restrict fake nodes from linking to honest peers. An attacker must commit scarce capital into staking bilateral credit edges for every identity spawned. However, a sudden tide of colluding bridge nodes can saturate cut capacity, allowing fraudulent agents to slip through.
